summary: Initial security posture intake for inference deployment. Customer wants clear KMS/bring-your-own-key options, SSO/SAML and RBAC integration details, audit log retention, and recommendations on hosted vs dedicated vs private given PCI/PA-DSS considerations. Agreed to follow up with artifacts and a technical deep dive for deployment planning.
topics: RBAC and least privilege for inference endpoints
Audit logs, retention windows, and exportability
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Data residency and retention for transactional PII
questions: Can audit logs be shipped to our SIEM in near real-time?
How does RBAC map to our existing Okta groups?
What's the default data retention for request/response logs?
If we go Private on-prem, what networking/network isolation is required?
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: hi everyone thanks for making time today, i know it's a busy week 00:05 Rajiv Patel: hey thanks, appreciate it 00:09 Maya Chen: quick intros — i'm maya on account side, leo from our solutions engineering team will cover the technicals 00:15 Leo Ortiz: hi all, leo ortiz redwood se, i'd say we'll go through security posture then open to specific infra questions 00:22 Sofia Alvarez: great, our goal today is to understand whether we can run with Hosted or if we need Dedicated or Private — and the gating security controls 00:32 Tom Greene: also want operational stuff, like audit-logs export, retention, and how keys are handled 00:40 Maya Chen: perfect, we'll tackle those in order. can you give quick context on data types and compliance? 00:47 Rajiv Patel: yes so emeraldbay is retail focused, we process orders, returns, and customer support chat. we have PII in some support transcripts — names, emails, partial cc last4, nothing full cc on chat side, but payments go through our payment processors and some metadata touches us. we are PCI sensitive and also have SOC2 requirements from a number of partners 01:10 Leo Ortiz: ok that helps. couple of clarifying q's — are you considering Redwood for customer-facing generation in prod or for internal tooling first? 01:18 Aisha Khan: internal first: agent for CS triage and suggested answers, then potentially customer-facing for dynamic suggestions. timeline 3-6 months for pilot 01:27 Maya Chen: understood. on compliance — we are SOC2 Type II and have ISO 27001 mappings; we can share artifacts. for customers that need BYOK we support integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS and customer HSMs via bring-your-own-key workflows 01:43 Rajiv Patel: when you say BYOK, do you hold any key material at rest? what is the key lifecycle? 01:49 Leo Ortiz: good question — our hosted product supports envelope encryption where you supply a KMS key and we use it to wrap data keys; we do not store your raw key material. for Private/on-prem deployments you control the full key lifecycle. i should note sometimes transcription labels confuse kv cache as kv cash in the notes — just a common ASR quirk — but KV cache we could persist encrypted in ephemeral storage depending on deployment mode 02:12 Tom Greene: about audit logs, can we stream them to our splunk or do you ingest and hold them? 02:18 Leo Ortiz: we can stream syslog/json events via a delivery connector to your SIEM in near real-time for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has an export pipeline — default retention 90d on hosted for request/metadata but you can configure longer retention with enterprise add-ons or route to your storage. 02:36 Rajiv Patel: 90 days default might be a concern; for SOC2 audits we want 12 months of certain logs. 02:42 Maya Chen: that's fine — we can map which logs are required for your audits and either extend retention on hosted or ship logs to your storage for indefinite retention. will follow up with mapping doc 02:55 Aisha Khan: SSO — we use Okta, and groups determine access to environments. can redwood map Okta groups to RBAC roles? 03:03 Leo Ortiz: yes, SAML inbound via Okta supported. we map SAML group claims to RBAC roles in the console; RBAC is role and scope based, you can limit token creation, model deployment, and route access. 03:17 Tom Greene: can we enforce least privilege on per-route basis? e.g., only a small set of services can call the high-sensitivity model endpoints 03:24 Leo Ortiz: absolutely — policy rules can be scoped by route/model/environment. you can also create service principals for CI/CD with limited permissions. 03:31 Rajiv Patel: encryption at-rest — do you encrypt model weights? and what about logs that contain PII? 03:37 Leo Ortiz: model weights are encrypted at rest in our managed clusters for Hosted and Dedicated variants. for Private/on-prem you manage encryption. logs that contain PII we recommend tokenization or routing to your controlled storage; we can obfuscate certain fields pre-ingest if needed but that adds latency so we'll discuss tradeoffs 03:58 Maya Chen: quick commercial note — Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and more options for retention and log streaming; Private is full control but longer setup 04:06 Rajiv Patel: is there a SOC2/ISO attestation we can get right away? we need to show auditors 04:11 Maya Chen: yes we'll send SOC2 Type II report summary and ISO 27001 scope doc. i'll drop links after the call 04:17 Sofia Alvarez: about network — if we were to do Private on-prem, what's required on our side? firewall/NAT, ports? 04:23 Leo Ortiz: for on-prem we have a short ops checklist: outbound access to our control plane or air-gapped mode where control plane runs locally. typical ports are 443 for control and 5222 for some internal comms in older setups, but i'll send exact list. in VPC mode you can peer or use private endpoints. 04:40 Tom Greene: latency — for customer-facing generation, we need <200ms per request 04:46 Leo Ortiz: latency SLA depends on model size and pool sizing. Dedicated pools can be tuned for low-latency; we also have optimized kernels and batching options. if strict <200ms for 0.5k qps we'd recommend dedicated pinned capacity. 04:59 Rajiv Patel: data residency — some EU customers require data not leave eu-west-1 05:04 Maya Chen: we have region pinning in Hosted and Dedicated. Private obviously stays on your network. 05:10 Aisha Khan: retention policy question — what is redwood's policy-or-default for request/response content used for model improvement? do you train on customer data? 05:19 Leo Ortiz: short answer: we don't use customer request/response for model training by default. customers can opt-in to share telemetry for product improvement but for enterprise customers that is off. we'll include language in the contract and the DPA. 05:32 Rajiv Patel: great, need explicit contract language for no-training clause and data handling 05:36 Maya Chen: we'll add that to the security and legal package. 05:39 Sofia Alvarez: can you show how RBAC and SAML work in console — maybe in the technical deep dive? 05:44 Leo Ortiz: yes, we'll demo mapping Okta groups, show audit log export config, and walkthrough KMS integration for a mock key in the next session 05:52 Tom Greene: one other — retention of KV cache, since we might use cached embeddings that reference PII — how long is that cached and is it encryptable? 05:59 Leo Ortiz: KV cache lifetime is configurable; for Hosted we rotate cache shards and persist encrypted. we can also advise evicting caches on sensitive routes. encryption is supported at rest; for extra assurance you can use private deployment and control the storage lifecycle 06:18 Rajiv Patel: any PCI-specific guidance? most of our card flows hit payment processors but logs can contain tokens 06:25 Leo Ortiz: we recommend minimizing card data anywhere in prompts; use tokenization and redaction on ingest. for PCI, Private deployment is the most conservative route since you can control all flow. Dedicated with strict network controls is a middle ground. 06:38 Maya Chen: ok let's recap next steps 06:41 Maya Chen: maya will email SOC2 and ISO artifacts, leo will prep on-prem ops checklist and demo plan, tom will send required retention lists, and we'll schedule the technical deep dive 06:51 Rajiv Patel: sounds good thanks everyone 06:53 Maya Chen: thank you all, we'll follow up with times for the deep dive and the files 06:56 Aisha Khan: thanks 06:57 Sofia Alvarez: bye everyone
